world_offer_label: the Hieronymian world of Jerome, Paula, and the Bethlehem ascetic-literary community
_comment: Primary-text translations and secondary scholarship drawn from this world's own vetted Source Registry / Doc_02, curated for a participant who wants to go deeper after talking with this world's Representative.

resources.title: Jerome: His Life, Writings, and Controversies
resources.author: J.N.D. Kelly
resources.note: The classic, readable biography of Jerome — a good starting point for the whole scholarly-ascetic circle at Bethlehem, though later scholarship (Cain, Clark) complicates its more Jerome-trusting picture.

resources.title: Jerome
resources.author: Stefan Rebenich
resources.note: A compact introduction pairing Jerome's own patronage-and-authority dynamics with translated excerpts from his letters — useful for seeing how he positioned himself among wealthy Christian patrons like Paula and Marcella.

resources.title: The Origenist Controversy: The Cultural Construction of an Early Christian Debate
resources.author: Elizabeth A. Clark
resources.note: The key methodological study of how elite women like Paula, Eustochium, and Marcella become recoverable at all only through male-authored texts — directly relevant to how this world's Representative asks you to read its own sources.

resources.title: The Letters of Jerome: Asceticism, Biblical Exegesis, and the Construction of Christian Authority in Late Antiquity
resources.author: Andrew Cain
resources.note: The critical-edition backbone behind this world's own confidence calibration — reads Jerome's letters and epitaphs for Paula and Marcella as self-conscious rhetorical constructions of his own authority, not neutral biography.

resources.title: Select Letters and Works of Jerome (including the Epitaph on Paula, Ep. 108)
resources.author: Jerome
resources.publisher: Nicene and Post-Nicene Fathers, Second Series, Vol. 6
resources.note: A public-domain nineteenth-century translation, freely available online, of Jerome's own letters — including his obituary for Paula, the single richest surviving account of her life and the Bethlehem community.
